notes: PAY TWO REMITTANCE RUNS WITH ONE CHEQUE, AND HAVE THE REGISTER SAY SO. If you remit withholdings and enter a cheque number the register already holds, MoRaj Ledger used to refuse it and send you to a fresh number. But when you really had written ONE cheque covering both runs, you wrote it regardless — and the register kept only the first run's figure. Every bank reconciliation after that understated your unpresented cheques by the difference, and the only way to sign the month off was to force it with an adjustment. Now it ASKS. You are shown what that number already stands for, to whom, and what the register will read if these deductions are added to it. Yes, and the register holds what the cheque genuinely paid. No, and nothing is posted — you are told to enter the number of the cheque you actually wrote. It is never decided for you, because a repeated cheque number is also precisely what a mistyped one looks like. EVERY DEDUCTION KEEPS ITS OWN WITHHOLDING CERTIFICATE — its own payee, its own TIN, its own amount, each printable on its own exactly as before. A certificate belongs to the person the tax was withheld from, never to the cheque that happened to settle it. CORRECT A CHEQUE'S REGISTERED AMOUNT. Cheque Register → CORRECT AMOUNT on any cheque that is not cancelled. It asks what the cheque was written for — offering the figure your own remittance records say it settled — and asks why, which is kept on the audit trail. This changes the REGISTER ONLY and posts nothing to your ledger, because in this situation the ledger is already correct: the money left the bank properly and it was the register that fell short. Use it to put right anything entered before this release. AND THE APP NOW TELLS YOU WHEN THEY DISAGREE. The alert banner compares what your remittance records say each cheque settled with what the cheque register holds, and names any cheque where the two do not match — so a reconciliation that will not tie explains itself instead of leaving you hunting. This release includes a database change. Please take a backup before you upgrade.
